strategies.title: Funding basis
strategies.description:
Holds the spot asset and shorts the perpetual against it, so the position has no view on the price, and collects the funding the shorts are paid while the perpetual trades above the spot. When funding falls far enough it unwinds, and when the vault falls far enough from its peak it only reduces.

The edge is mechanical and it compresses as more capital chases it, which is the honest thing to say about it: the record shows the size it was earned at, and a larger vault should expect less.
claims: Gross exposure at most twice the vault's value
No single order above 5% of the vault
5% of the vault kept liquid, so an ordinary withdrawal closes nothing
Only reduces after a 10% fall from the vault's peak
One market, BTC against BTC-PERP, and nothing else
strategies.author: shonin

[workspace]
resolver = "3"
members = ["packages/agents/funding-basis"]

[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.98"
license = "Apache-2.0"
publish = false

[workspace.dependencies]
# The SDK an agent is written against. It is declared by version, and a
# local checkout is patched in through .cargo/config.toml while both move
# together; the build service supplies its own pinned copy the same way, so
# `--locked` holds on both sides.
shonin-strategy-sdk = "0.1.0"

futures = "0.3.34"
serde = { version = "1.0.229", features = ["derive"] }

[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "deny"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }

[profile.release]
# An agent is a component the build service compiles from source with a
# pinned recipe, so the profile is part of what makes it reproducible.
opt-level = "s"
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
strip = true

[package]
name = "funding-basis"
description = "Holds spot, shorts the perp, and collects the funding between them"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
publish.workspace = true

[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]

[dependencies]
futures.workspace = true
shonin-strategy-sdk.workspace = true

[lints]
workspace = true

[vault]
chain = "base"

[description]
title = "Funding basis"
text = """
Holds the spot asset and shorts the perpetual against it, so the position has \
no view on the price, and collects the funding the shorts are paid while the \
perpetual trades above the spot. When funding falls far enough it unwinds, \
and when the vault falls far enough from its peak it only reduces.

The edge is mechanical and it compresses as more capital chases it, which is \
the honest thing to say about it: the record shows the size it was earned at, \
and a larger vault should expect less.
"""
claims = [
    "Gross exposure at most twice the vault's value",
    "No single order above 5% of the vault",
    "5% of the vault kept liquid, so an ordinary withdrawal closes nothing",
    "Only reduces after a 10% fall from the vault's peak",
    "One market, BTC against BTC-PERP, and nothing else",
]

[drivers.local]

# Pinned to an exact stable release so every machine and the reproducible
# executor image build with the same compiler. Bump deliberately.
[toolchain]
channel = "1.98.1"
components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"]
targets = ["wasm32-unknown-unknown", "wasm32-wasip2"]

legs.key: an agent the vault approved, trade-only

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop high-water mark (`peak`) lives only in process memory and is reset to zero on every restart, so a crash or redeploy silently clears the vault's historical peak and can cancel the claimed 10% drawdown-stop protection.
findings.detail: `Mind::new()` sets `peak: zero()` (lib.rs:86-87), and `step()` only ever raises `peak` when it observes a higher `state.vault_value` (lib.rs:140-142) — it never reads a historical high-water mark from the venue or vault. The module doc for `Mind` explicitly claims the opposite: 'It is rebuilt from the venue whenever it runs, so losing it to a restart costs a moment and nothing else' (lib.rs:37-38). That is true for position state (which is re-read from the venue each step) but false for `peak`: if the vault had fallen 10%+ from a true peak and the agent was correctly in reduce-only mode, a restart makes the new instance's `peak` equal to the current (already-depressed) value, `only_reducing` immediately evaluates to false, and the agent resumes opening new positions exactly when the manifest claims it should only be reducing.

findings.summary: Both legs of the spot/perp carry are submitted together but the fill verdicts are discarded, so a partial fill (one leg filled, the other rejected) leaves a naked directional position the code has no path to detect or unwind.
findings.detail: `open_one_step` submits a spot buy and a perp sell as one batch and the comment asserts 'the venue answers for both together' (lib.rs:217-219), but `submit()` discards the `Vec<Verdict>` entirely (`.map(|_| ())`, lib.rs:337-340) — neither the per-order nor per-batch result is ever inspected. If one leg fills and the other does not (an ordinary venue outcome: partial fills, one-sided rejects, rate limits), the account genuinely holds a one-sided position. The only path back to flat, `unwind_one_step`, is gated on `carrying = position(spot) > 0 && position(perp) < 0` (lib.rs:155-156, 159-160); an orphaned single leg makes `carrying` false, so the strategy never recognizes it as something to close and instead keeps evaluating `open_one_step` again (sized off `gross_notional`, which only measures magnitude, not direction). The position sits unhedged — the exact outcome the strategy's whole design exists to avoid — until a full halt triggers `flatten()`.

findings.summary: The claim 'No single order above 5% of the vault' is explicitly lifted to 100% of the vault during a halt, with no carve-out stated in shonin.toml.
findings.detail: `flatten()` builds a modified `Limits` with `max_order_fraction: Decimal::from(1)` (lib.rs:286-289) before unwinding, specifically to close the book faster when the vault is halting. The reasoning in the comment is sound (a wide fill beats a stuck leg), and since every order here is `reduce_only`, it cannot increase risk beyond the position already held — but it is a literal, undisclosed exception to a claim stated in `shonin.toml` without qualification ('No single order above 5% of the vault').

findings.summary: Whether the claimed 2x gross-leverage and 5% per-order caps are actually enforced on the opening path can't be confirmed from this source, because the enforcement logic lives in the external, unincluded `shonin-strategy-sdk` crate.
findings.detail: `open_one_step` computes a `wanted` notional and hands it to `sdk::size_for(wanted, vault_value, gross, &mind.limits, minimum_notional)` (lib.rs:187-193), but `size_for`'s body, and the `Limits` type it consumes, are defined in `shonin-strategy-sdk`, which is pulled in only as a version-pinned dependency (Cargo.toml:17) and is not part of the submitted source. The agent crate itself never re-checks the resulting order against `max_gross_leverage` or `max_order_fraction` after `size_for` returns, so the two headline risk claims rest entirely on code outside this review.

review.summary: A single long-lived async loop that holds spot BTC, shorts BTC-PERP against it, and nets the funding spread. It re-reads account state from the venue on every wakeup (good restart hygiene for positions), opens in one two-leg submission when funding clears an entry threshold, unwinds perp-first-then-spot when funding drops or the vault is in drawdown, and flattens fully on a vault halt. The five claimed limits (2x gross leverage, 5% per-order cap, 5% idle buffer, 10%-drawdown-stop, BTC/BTC-PERP only) are all represented as named constants in config.rs and threaded through the code, and a unit test ties the manifest wording to those constants. Two things undercut the safety story on a close read: the drawdown-stop's high-water mark is kept only in memory and silently resets on restart, and the two-leg order submission discards its fill verdicts, so a partial fill could leave a naked, undetected position. No malicious code, backdoors, reviewer-directed text, hidden date/address logic, or ML-driven sizing were found.
limits: The `shonin-strategy-sdk` crate (Decimal, Limits, size_for, drivers::*, vault::* and their guarantees around atomic multi-action submission) is not part of this submission; the review can confirm only that this agent calls into it with the stated constants, not what that code actually enforces.
The real venue/market behind the 'local' driver named in shonin.toml, and that market's liquidity and who controls its price feed, is outside this source.
The `.cargo/config.toml` patch mentioned in Cargo.toml's comments (which is said to pin the SDK checkout) was not supplied, so the reproducibility of the SDK dependency itself can't be checked.
This is a static reading of the source only: the code was not compiled, run, or tested against a venue, and no runtime, fuzzing, or historical-performance evidence was used.

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop's reference point ('peak') is kept only in memory and resets on restart, voiding the 10%-from-peak guarantee.
findings.detail: Mind::new() initializes peak to zero(). On every process start, run() calls step() first, which sets mind.peak = state.vault_value because any positive value exceeds the zero starting peak. If the vault has already drawn down significantly before a restart, the real historical peak is lost and replaced by the (lower) current value, so only_reducing() will not fire again until a fresh 10% drop from this new, artificially low peak — even though the manifest claims the agent 'only reduces after a 10% fall from the vault's peak' with no restart caveat. The doc comment on Mind ('losing it to a restart costs a moment and nothing else') is incorrect for this field specifically, since peak cannot be rebuilt from venue state the way positions can.

findings.summary: flatten() removes the 5%-of-vault per-order cap during a halt, contradicting the stated claim.
findings.detail: flatten() constructs a Limits value with max_order_fraction overridden to Decimal::from(1) (100%) and uses it for every unwind_one_step call during a halt. The manifest's claim 'No single order above 5% of the vault' is stated without exception, but the code itself departs from it in the halt path. The rationale given in the comment (avoid leaving a leg on at the cost of a wider fill) may be reasonable, but it is not disclosed as an exception to the claim.

findings.summary: Order submission results are discarded, so rejections or partial two-leg fills are never checked or logged.
findings.detail: submit() returns Ok(drivers::submit(...).await) and both open_one_step and unwind_one_step map that Vec<Verdict> away with `.map(|_| ())`. The comment at the two-leg submission in open_one_step assumes the venue fills both legs together or neither; nothing in this source verifies that, and if a leg is rejected while the other fills, the resulting naked exposure is only caught implicitly, by waiting for another venue event to trigger the next step().

review.summary: A delta-neutral BTC funding-basis carry agent: holds spot BTC long and shorts BTC-PERP in equal notional, opens more when funding exceeds an entry threshold and unwinds when funding falls below an exit threshold or the vault has drawn down 10% from its peak. Every step re-reads true account state from the venue rather than trusting in-memory state, sizes new orders through the SDK's shared limit function plus a local 5%-of-vault per-order cap on the unwind path, and keeps an idle buffer at home so an ordinary withdrawal doesn't force a close. On a halt signal it flattens both legs reduce-only, with its own per-order cap explicitly lifted for that path. The most consequential fact in the source is that the 'peak' used for the drawdown stop lives only in memory and resets to the current vault value on every restart, so the 10%-from-peak guarantee does not survive a restart.
limits: The implementation of `shonin-strategy-sdk` (size_for's actual enforcement of the 2x gross-leverage cap, and the real semantics of drivers::* and vault::events()) is an external dependency, not part of the submitted source, so its enforcement of the claimed limits could not be verified directly, only that this agent passes the right constants into it.

The venue behind the 'local' driver named in shonin.toml — its liquidity, who can move its price, and whether it truly provides atomic multi-leg fills — lives in the platform's driver configuration, not shown here.
No backtest or funding-rate history was supplied, so the claimed mechanical edge and its compression with size could not be checked against evidence, only against the code's logic.
This is one reading of the code on a single date, not a proof the program is free of bugs or will behave this way under every runtime condition.

text = """

and when the vault falls far enough from its peak it only reduces.

the honest thing to say about it: the record shows the size it was earned at, \

review.summary: A single long-lived Rust agent that holds BTC spot and shorts BTC-PERP against it in matched notional, so it has no price view: it only collects funding while the perpetual trades above spot. It wakes on venue account events and vault events (never polling), opens when funding clears an entry threshold, unwinds when funding drops below a lower exit threshold, and rebalances toward 80% deployment one bounded step at a time. Position sizing for new carry is delegated to the SDK's size_for with the agent's own Limits (2x gross leverage, 5% per order, 5% idle buffer); unwinding caps itself independently via cap_by_notional. Drawdown protection switches the agent to reduce-only once the vault is 10% below the highest value this running instance has observed - a peak kept only in memory. On a vault Halting event it tries up to 32 steps to flatten both legs, lifting its own 5% order cap to do so, then exits and leaves anything left to the vault contract's own reduce-only close. The constants in config.rs line up with the claims in shonin.toml and are cross-checked by a unit test.
limits: The shonin-strategy-sdk crate (size_for, Limits, drivers::*, vault::*, Decimal) is an external, version-pinned dependency; its source was not included, so the mechanics that actually enforce max_gross_leverage, max_order_fraction and idle_buffer when opening a position could not be read.

What the 'local' driver and the Base-chain vault contract actually are and do in production - venue identity and liquidity, how a halt or a depositor claim is executed on-chain - is outside this source and could not be checked.
No logs, backtests, or live trading history were supplied; this is one static reading of the source, not a test under real market conditions or a proof that the strategy is safe or profitable.
The .cargo/config.toml patch pinning the local SDK checkout was not shown, so the exact SDK revision this agent would build against is unknown.

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop high-water mark (`peak`) lives only in process memory and is reset to zero on every restart, so a crash or redeploy silently clears the vault's historical peak and can cancel the claimed 10% drawdown-stop protection.
findings.detail: `Mind::new()` sets `peak: zero()` (lib.rs:86-87), and `step()` only ever raises `peak` when it observes a higher `state.vault_value` (lib.rs:140-142) — it never reads a historical high-water mark from the venue or vault. The module doc for `Mind` explicitly claims the opposite: 'It is rebuilt from the venue whenever it runs, so losing it to a restart costs a moment and nothing else' (lib.rs:37-38). That is true for position state (which is re-read from the venue each step) but false for `peak`: if the vault had fallen 10%+ from a true peak and the agent was correctly in reduce-only mode, a restart makes the new instance's `peak` equal to the current (already-depressed) value, `only_reducing` immediately evaluates to false, and the agent resumes opening new positions exactly when the manifest claims it should only be reducing.

findings.summary: Both legs of the spot/perp carry are submitted together but the fill verdicts are discarded, so a partial fill (one leg filled, the other rejected) leaves a naked directional position the code has no path to detect or unwind.
findings.detail: `open_one_step` submits a spot buy and a perp sell as one batch and the comment asserts 'the venue answers for both together' (lib.rs:217-219), but `submit()` discards the `Vec<Verdict>` entirely (`.map(|_| ())`, lib.rs:337-340) — neither the per-order nor per-batch result is ever inspected. If one leg fills and the other does not (an ordinary venue outcome: partial fills, one-sided rejects, rate limits), the account genuinely holds a one-sided position. The only path back to flat, `unwind_one_step`, is gated on `carrying = position(spot) > 0 && position(perp) < 0` (lib.rs:155-156, 159-160); an orphaned single leg makes `carrying` false, so the strategy never recognizes it as something to close and instead keeps evaluating `open_one_step` again (sized off `gross_notional`, which only measures magnitude, not direction). The position sits unhedged — the exact outcome the strategy's whole design exists to avoid — until a full halt triggers `flatten()`.

findings.summary: The claim 'No single order above 5% of the vault' is explicitly lifted to 100% of the vault during a halt, with no carve-out stated in shonin.toml.
findings.detail: `flatten()` builds a modified `Limits` with `max_order_fraction: Decimal::from(1)` (lib.rs:286-289) before unwinding, specifically to close the book faster when the vault is halting. The reasoning in the comment is sound (a wide fill beats a stuck leg), and since every order here is `reduce_only`, it cannot increase risk beyond the position already held — but it is a literal, undisclosed exception to a claim stated in `shonin.toml` without qualification ('No single order above 5% of the vault').

findings.summary: Whether the claimed 2x gross-leverage and 5% per-order caps are actually enforced on the opening path can't be confirmed from this source, because the enforcement logic lives in the external, unincluded `shonin-strategy-sdk` crate.
findings.detail: `open_one_step` computes a `wanted` notional and hands it to `sdk::size_for(wanted, vault_value, gross, &mind.limits, minimum_notional)` (lib.rs:187-193), but `size_for`'s body, and the `Limits` type it consumes, are defined in `shonin-strategy-sdk`, which is pulled in only as a version-pinned dependency (Cargo.toml:17) and is not part of the submitted source. The agent crate itself never re-checks the resulting order against `max_gross_leverage` or `max_order_fraction` after `size_for` returns, so the two headline risk claims rest entirely on code outside this review.

review.summary: A single long-lived async loop that holds spot BTC, shorts BTC-PERP against it, and nets the funding spread. It re-reads account state from the venue on every wakeup (good restart hygiene for positions), opens in one two-leg submission when funding clears an entry threshold, unwinds perp-first-then-spot when funding drops or the vault is in drawdown, and flattens fully on a vault halt. The five claimed limits (2x gross leverage, 5% per-order cap, 5% idle buffer, 10%-drawdown-stop, BTC/BTC-PERP only) are all represented as named constants in config.rs and threaded through the code, and a unit test ties the manifest wording to those constants. Two things undercut the safety story on a close read: the drawdown-stop's high-water mark is kept only in memory and silently resets on restart, and the two-leg order submission discards its fill verdicts, so a partial fill could leave a naked, undetected position. No malicious code, backdoors, reviewer-directed text, hidden date/address logic, or ML-driven sizing were found.
limits: The `shonin-strategy-sdk` crate (Decimal, Limits, size_for, drivers::*, vault::* and their guarantees around atomic multi-action submission) is not part of this submission; the review can confirm only that this agent calls into it with the stated constants, not what that code actually enforces.
The real venue/market behind the 'local' driver named in shonin.toml, and that market's liquidity and who controls its price feed, is outside this source.
The `.cargo/config.toml` patch mentioned in Cargo.toml's comments (which is said to pin the SDK checkout) was not supplied, so the reproducibility of the SDK dependency itself can't be checked.
This is a static reading of the source only: the code was not compiled, run, or tested against a venue, and no runtime, fuzzing, or historical-performance evidence was used.

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop's reference point ('peak') is kept only in memory and resets on restart, voiding the 10%-from-peak guarantee.
findings.detail: Mind::new() initializes peak to zero(). On every process start, run() calls step() first, which sets mind.peak = state.vault_value because any positive value exceeds the zero starting peak. If the vault has already drawn down significantly before a restart, the real historical peak is lost and replaced by the (lower) current value, so only_reducing() will not fire again until a fresh 10% drop from this new, artificially low peak — even though the manifest claims the agent 'only reduces after a 10% fall from the vault's peak' with no restart caveat. The doc comment on Mind ('losing it to a restart costs a moment and nothing else') is incorrect for this field specifically, since peak cannot be rebuilt from venue state the way positions can.

findings.summary: flatten() removes the 5%-of-vault per-order cap during a halt, contradicting the stated claim.
findings.detail: flatten() constructs a Limits value with max_order_fraction overridden to Decimal::from(1) (100%) and uses it for every unwind_one_step call during a halt. The manifest's claim 'No single order above 5% of the vault' is stated without exception, but the code itself departs from it in the halt path. The rationale given in the comment (avoid leaving a leg on at the cost of a wider fill) may be reasonable, but it is not disclosed as an exception to the claim.

findings.summary: Order submission results are discarded, so rejections or partial two-leg fills are never checked or logged.
findings.detail: submit() returns Ok(drivers::submit(...).await) and both open_one_step and unwind_one_step map that Vec<Verdict> away with `.map(|_| ())`. The comment at the two-leg submission in open_one_step assumes the venue fills both legs together or neither; nothing in this source verifies that, and if a leg is rejected while the other fills, the resulting naked exposure is only caught implicitly, by waiting for another venue event to trigger the next step().

review.summary: A delta-neutral BTC funding-basis carry agent: holds spot BTC long and shorts BTC-PERP in equal notional, opens more when funding exceeds an entry threshold and unwinds when funding falls below an exit threshold or the vault has drawn down 10% from its peak. Every step re-reads true account state from the venue rather than trusting in-memory state, sizes new orders through the SDK's shared limit function plus a local 5%-of-vault per-order cap on the unwind path, and keeps an idle buffer at home so an ordinary withdrawal doesn't force a close. On a halt signal it flattens both legs reduce-only, with its own per-order cap explicitly lifted for that path. The most consequential fact in the source is that the 'peak' used for the drawdown stop lives only in memory and resets to the current vault value on every restart, so the 10%-from-peak guarantee does not survive a restart.
limits: The implementation of `shonin-strategy-sdk` (size_for's actual enforcement of the 2x gross-leverage cap, and the real semantics of drivers::* and vault::events()) is an external dependency, not part of the submitted source, so its enforcement of the claimed limits could not be verified directly, only that this agent passes the right constants into it.

The venue behind the 'local' driver named in shonin.toml — its liquidity, who can move its price, and whether it truly provides atomic multi-leg fills — lives in the platform's driver configuration, not shown here.
No backtest or funding-rate history was supplied, so the claimed mechanical edge and its compression with size could not be checked against evidence, only against the code's logic.
This is one reading of the code on a single date, not a proof the program is free of bugs or will behave this way under every runtime condition.

findings.summary: The drawdown-stop high-water mark lives only in process memory and resets to the current vault value on every restart, silently re-arming the stop.
findings.detail: `Mind.peak` (lib.rs:44) starts at `zero()` in `Mind::new()` (lib.rs:87) and is only ever raised from the first `read_state()` after the process starts (lib.rs:140-142: `if state.vault_value > mind.peak { mind.peak = state.vault_value }`). `only_reducing()` (lib.rs:92-94) — the sole gate for the claimed '10% fall from the vault's peak' stop — is measured entirely against this session-local value. If the agent restarts (deploy, crash, OOM, upgrade) while the vault is already below its true all-time peak, the new peak is set to whatever the vault is worth at that moment, discarding the drawdown already incurred. The vault would need to fall a further 10% from that new, lower baseline before the stop fires again, even though the manifest's claim ('when the vault falls far enough from its peak it only reduces') reads as an all-time guarantee. The doc comment at lib.rs:42-43 ('the most the vault has been worth while this instance watched it') acknowledges this is session-scoped, but that qualifier doesn't appear in `shonin.toml`'s claim or in `config.rs`'s comment for `DRAWDOWN_STOP`.

findings.summary: Submitted order verdicts are discarded, so a one-sided fill of the paired spot/perp orders is never explicitly detected or reconciled outside the drawdown/halt paths.
findings.detail: `submit()` (lib.rs:337-339) returns the venue's `Vec<Verdict>`, but `open_one_step` (lib.rs:220-238) throws the result away with `.map(|_| ())`, and nothing else inspects whether either leg of the paired buy/sell was rejected. The comment at lib.rs:217-219 states plainly that a filled long beside an unfilled short 'is a directional bet, which is the one thing this strategy never means to hold' — yet `carrying` (lib.rs:155-156) requires both legs to be present (`position(spot) > 0 && position(perp) < 0`) to take the unwind branch. If a partial fill leaves one leg naked, `carrying` is false, `only_reducing` is false (absent an unrelated drawdown), and `step()` falls through to `open_one_step` again, which can add a fresh hedged pair on top of the orphaned leg rather than closing it. The only paths that would fully flatten such an orphan are a drawdown-stop (`unwind_one_step` runs on any held spot/perp position regardless of `carrying`) or a vault halt (`flatten`), not ordinary operation.

findings.summary: A single failed account-state read terminates the whole agent loop, with no retry or backoff, which compounds the peak-reset issue above.
findings.detail: `read_state()` (lib.rs:168-170) propagates any error from `drivers::account_state(...).await?` straight up; `step()` (lib.rs:138-139) does the same with `read_state().await?`; and `run()`'s initial call (lib.rs:110) and its event loop (lib.rs:118-132) both propagate that `Result` out of the agent entirely via `?`. There is no retry or backoff around a single transient read failure before the process exits. Combined with the restart-unsafe peak in `Mind` (lib.rs:44), a transient venue hiccup that trips this path would restart the agent and quietly discard the drawdown high-water mark along with it.

findings.summary: The opening-side enforcement of the claimed 2x gross-leverage and 5%-per-order caps is delegated to `size_for`, a function not included in the submitted source.
findings.detail: `open_one_step` computes the notional to trade via `size_for(wanted, state.vault_value, gross, &mind.limits, mind.settings.minimum_notional)` (lib.rs:187-193), passing `mind.limits` (built from `config::MAX_GROSS_LEVERAGE` and `config::MAX_ORDER_FRACTION` at lib.rs:65-72). `size_for` itself lives in the `shonin-strategy-sdk` crate, which this project depends on by version (Cargo.toml:17) but does not include — so whether it actually clamps to those limits cannot be confirmed by reading this project alone. By contrast, the unwind/close path enforces its own per-order cap directly and visibly in this file (`cap_by_notional`, lib.rs:326-332, applied at lib.rs:250-255), and the idle-buffer claim is likewise enforced directly and visibly (lib.rs:201-215). The gap is specific to the opening-side leverage/order-size caps.

findings.summary: The manifest names only an empty `[drivers.local]` table, so the actual venue and price/funding feed behind the BTC/BTC-PERP market are not specified anywhere in the submitted project.
findings.detail: `DRIVER` is the literal string `"local"` (lib.rs:29), and the manifest's driver section is empty (`[drivers.local]` with no fields, shonin.toml:24). All prices, funding rates and fills the agent acts on (`perp.funding_fraction()`, `spot.ask`, `perp.bid`, etc.) come through this named driver, whose concrete implementation, venue and feed source are outside this project. The agent's actual exposure to thin-liquidity or feed-manipulation risk (relevant to the 'one market, BTC against BTC-PERP' claim) therefore cannot be assessed from this source alone.

findings.detail: A venue error rejects one leg of a two-order submission without generating a further account event. The strategy has no record it was rejected and nothing in this code retries or alerts; it waits on the next unrelated event to resync from read_state().

findings.summary: Gross-leverage and per-order caps for opening a position are enforced only inside the external size_for function, not in this submitted source.
findings.detail: A reader trying to confirm from this project alone that MAX_GROSS_LEVERAGE or MAX_ORDER_FRACTION bound an opening order cannot: open_one_step() hands wanted, vault_value, gross and &mind.limits to size_for() and trusts the return value, and size_for's implementation lives in the unincluded shonin-strategy-sdk dependency.

review.summary: A single long-lived Rust agent that holds BTC spot and shorts BTC-PERP against it in matched notional, so it has no price view: it only collects funding while the perpetual trades above spot. It wakes on venue account events and vault events (never polling), opens when funding clears an entry threshold, unwinds when funding drops below a lower exit threshold, and rebalances toward 80% deployment one bounded step at a time. Position sizing for new carry is delegated to the SDK's size_for with the agent's own Limits (2x gross leverage, 5% per order, 5% idle buffer); unwinding caps itself independently via cap_by_notional. Drawdown protection switches the agent to reduce-only once the vault is 10% below the highest value this running instance has observed - a peak kept only in memory. On a vault Halting event it tries up to 32 steps to flatten both legs, lifting its own 5% order cap to do so, then exits and leaves anything left to the vault contract's own reduce-only close. The constants in config.rs line up with the claims in shonin.toml and are cross-checked by a unit test.
limits: The shonin-strategy-sdk crate (size_for, Limits, drivers::*, vault::*, Decimal) is an external, version-pinned dependency; its source was not included, so the mechanics that actually enforce max_gross_leverage, max_order_fraction and idle_buffer when opening a position could not be read.

What the 'local' driver and the Base-chain vault contract actually are and do in production - venue identity and liquidity, how a halt or a depositor claim is executed on-chain - is outside this source and could not be checked.
No logs, backtests, or live trading history were supplied; this is one static reading of the source, not a test under real market conditions or a proof that the strategy is safe or profitable.
The .cargo/config.toml patch pinning the local SDK checkout was not shown, so the exact SDK revision this agent would build against is unknown.
